bib.title: Scaling Synthetic Data Creation with 1,000,000,000 Personas

question: How can diverse synthetic data be created at billion scale when seed-instance and key-point prompting cannot scale in diversity?
hypothesis: Adding a persona to a data synthesis prompt steers an LLM to that perspective, so a collection of 1 billion personas yields diverse synthetic data at scale.
contributions: Persona-driven data synthesis methodology (zero-shot, few-shot, persona-enhanced few-shot prompts)
Persona Hub: 1,015,863,523 personas built by Text-to-Persona and Persona-to-Persona with deduplication
Use cases: math and logical reasoning problems, instructions, knowledge-rich texts, game NPCs, tools
Release of 200,000 personas and sample synthetic data

method.summary: Personas are inferred from RedPajama v2 web text by prompting an LLM, expanded through six rounds of relationship expansion and deduplicated. 1.09M math problems are synthesized with GPT-4 zero-shot persona prompts, solved by gpt-4o, and used to fine-tune Qwen2-7B, evaluated on a synthetic in-distribution test set and MATH.
method.task: persona-driven synthetic data creation; math reasoning SFT

datasets.name: Persona Hub
datasets.source: Text-to-Persona on RedPajama v2 then Persona-to-Persona (6 iterations)
datasets.preprocessing: MinHash dedup (1-gram, signature size 128, similarity threshold 0.9), then embedding dedup (text-embedding-3-small, cosine > 0.9), plus simple heuristic quality filters

datasets.name: Synthetic math problems
datasets.split: 20k held out as synthetic test set
datasets.source: 0-shot persona prompting with GPT-4 on 1.09 million personas; solutions by gpt-4o (assistant)

datasets.name: Synthetic test set
datasets.preprocessing: solutions from gpt-4o (assistant), gpt-4o (PoT) and gpt-4-turbo (assistant); kept only where at least two solutions consistent

datasets.name: MATH
datasets.preprocessing: no MATH instance used in synthesis or training

models.name: GPT-4 (problem creator; exact version not stated)

training.objective: inferred: supervised fine-tuning on synthesized problem-solution pairs (paper says 'fine-tune')

other.scaling: Fig 9 trains on different synthetic data scales; values not given in text

inference.decoding: greedy decoding for the fine-tuned model
inference.temperature: 0 (greedy) for persona-pair problem creation in similarity experiment
inference.samples: one greedy output per problem; no seeds or repeats stated
inference.prompting: 0-shot persona prompt 'Create a challenging math problem with the following persona' (simplified; paper says the prompts shown are not exactly those used)

parameters.persona_similarity_levels: 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 (100 pairs each), 0.9 for gpt-4o vs gpt-35-turbo

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: answer equality against reference; MATH uses OpenAI simple-evals protocol, synthetic test uses Llama-3-70B-Instruct as equality checker

metrics.name: Problem validity rate
metrics.definition: two math experts judge 200 sampled challenging problems

eval.protocol: Single run; no seeds or significance tests. Some MATH baseline numbers marked * may not use OpenAI evaluation method. Authors say in-distribution test is reference only.

availability.data: 200,000 personas and samples: 50,000 math problems, 50,000 instructions, 10,000 game NPCs, 50,000 logical reasoning problems, 10,000 knowledge-rich texts, 5,000 tools; 370M expert personas added Feb 2025. The 1.07M training set is not stated as released.

prompts.text: You are a helpful assistant. Guess a prompt (i.e., instruction) that the following persona may ask you to do: {persona}
Assume you are the persona described as follows. Write a Quora article using your knowledge, skills, experience, or insights.
Who is likely to [read|write|like|dislike|...] the text?
Who is in close relationship with the given persona?
Create a challenging math problem with the following persona: {persona}

results.claim: Qwen2-7B fine-tuned on 1.07M persona-synthesized math problems reaches 64.9% on MATH with greedy decoding, without any MATH data.
results.setup: Qwen2-7B SFT on 1.07M GPT-4-created, gpt-4o-solved problems; greedy decoding; OpenAI simple-evals equality check
results.quote: The 7B model fine-tuned with the synthetic training data achieved an impressive 64.9% accuracy on MATH simply using greedy decoding
results.table: Table 2, row Qwen2-7B (fine-tuned w/ the 1.07M synthesized instances), column Accuracy
results.note: Matches gpt-4-turbo-preview (1106 at 64.3, 0125 at 64.5); gpt-4o is 76.6.

results.claim: On the 11.6K in-distribution synthetic test set the fine-tuned model scores 79.4%, above all listed open-source LLMs but below GPT-4 variants.
results.setup: in-distribution; test answers filtered by agreement of two of three solutions; model trained on in-distribution data
results.table: Table 1, row Qwen2-7B (fine-tuned w/ the 1.07M synthesized instances), column Accuracy
results.note: Authors say it is reference only; gpt-4o scores 91.2 and gpt-4-turbo 88.1.

results.claim: Two math experts judged 193 of 200 sampled challenging synthesized problems valid.
results.setup: 200 sampled challenging problems (high school and university-level, China), two experts
results.quote: Only 7 out of 200 problems are marked as invalid (e.g., due to insufficient or conflicting conditions), yielding a reliable validity rate of 96.5%.

results.claim: Persona Hub contains over one billion personas after deduplication and filtering.
results.setup: Text-to-Persona on RedPajama v2, six rounds Persona-to-Persona, MinHash and embedding dedup at 0.9
results.quote: we have harvested a total of 1,015,863,523 personas, finally forming our Persona Hub.

results.claim: MATH accuracy rises with the amount of synthetic training data, roughly following a scaling law.
results.setup: Qwen2-7B trained on varying synthetic scale; values only in Fig 9
results.note: Claim: 'generally aligns with the scaling law (Kaplan et al., 2020)'; no fit given.

results.claim: Math problems created from persona pairs are less similar than the personas; gpt-4o and gpt-35-turbo problems from personas at 0.9 similarity mostly fall in 0.6 to 0.75.
results.setup: 100 persona pairs per similarity level, greedy decoding, text-embedding-3-small dim 512
results.quote: most synthesized math problems’ similarity falls within the range of 0.6 to 0.75, which is much lower than the similarity of the personas (0.9)

results.claim: Persona Hub is about 10^10 tokens, a 10,000x compression of public web text (10^14 tokens).

limits: Training hyperparameters (learning rate, epochs, batch size, hardware, optimizer) are not stated, so the 64.9% cannot be rerun from the paper.
Solutions come from gpt-4o, so the gain mixes persona-diverse problems with strong-teacher distillation; no ablation without personas or against a non-persona baseline is shown.
Diversity is argued from similarity of problem pairs only; no coverage or downstream ablation at billion scale.
In-distribution test answers are not fully reliable and only the authors' model trains in-distribution; authors say treat as reference.
Some baseline MATH numbers (*) may use a different evaluation method.
Only math is evaluated quantitatively; other use cases are qualitative examples, and prompts shown are simplified.
Authors concede persona descriptions lack fine-grained detail, text-only, and LLM hallucination limits fidelity.
Claims about eliminating the data bottleneck and mitigating model collapse are assertions without data.

terms.definition: Infer a persona likely to read, write, like or dislike a given text by prompting an LLM.
Derive personas with interpersonal relationships from existing personas, to reach low-visibility personas.
Few-shot prompt where each demonstration is paired with its derived persona.
